items.question: How does the AW169 RFM Section 7 describe the helicopter and its intended roles?
options: Medium twin-engine aircraft designed for land and sea operations including offshore services, HEMS, SAR, law enforcement, corporate and utility roles.
Light single-engine aircraft intended only for inland VFR training operations.
Heavy twin-engine aircraft certified exclusively for offshore oil and gas transport.
Single-engine helicopter optimised only for agricultural spraying and banner towing.
items.explanation: The opening paragraph of Section 7 Helicopter general describes the AW169 as a medium twin-engine aircraft for land and sea operations including offshore services, HEMS, SAR, law enforcement, corporate and utility roles.

items.question: According to Helicopter general in Section 7, what does the RFM state about the cockpit seats and flight controls?
options: Pilot and co-pilot have crashworthy seats and double commands (cyclic, collective bar and pedals).
Only the left seat is equipped with flight controls; the right seat is for passengers only.
Both seats are non-crashworthy and share a single set of flight controls.
The cockpit uses side-stick controllers with no conventional pedals.
items.explanation: Section 7 Helicopter general states that the cockpit has pilot and co-pilot crashworthy seats and double commands, including cyclic, collective bar and pedals for both crew members.

items.question: How is the main cabin structure described in the AW169 RFM Section 7?
options: Structure forward of the STA8175 joint with metallic internal structures and airframes and composite external fuselage skins, cowlings and fairings.
Entirely composite monocoque shell with no metallic internal structure.
All-metal stressed skin fuselage with no composite components.
Fabric-covered tubular frame with fixed landing gear attachments.
items.explanation: Section 7 states that the main cabin is the structure forward of the STA8175 joint, constructed of metallic internal structures and airframes with composite external fuselage skins, cowlings and fairings.

items.question: What is the primary structural feature of the AW169 tail unit according to Section 7?
options: Carbon fibre composite upper and lower longerons providing a continuous load path from the STA8175 joint to the fin.
Steel tube truss bolted directly to the main gearbox.
Aluminium honeycomb tail boom with no longerons.
Fabric-covered fin supported only by the tail rotor gearbox deck.
items.explanation: The Helicopter general text describes the tail unit primary structural parts as carbon fibre composite upper and lower longerons providing a continuous load path from the STA8175 joint to the fin.

items.question: Where are the circuit breaker panel and rotor brake control panel located in the AW169 cockpit?
options: In the overhead console above the heads of the flight crew.
On the left side of the main instrument panel.
On the rear cabin bulkhead behind the co-pilot.
Under the floor in the avionics bay.
items.explanation: Section 7 explains that the overhead console, installed above the heads of the flight crew, includes the circuit breaker panel and the rotor brake control panel.

items.question: According to Section 7, where are the control panels and displays that govern the installed systems and are used by the flight crew mainly located?
options: On the instrument panel and interseat console between the pilot and co-pilot.
Only on touchscreens in the rear cabin.
On the tail boom and external fuselage.
On the collective sticks exclusively.
items.explanation: The Helicopter general text states that the instrument panel and interseat console contain all the control panels and displays governing the systems installed in the aircraft and utilised by the flight crew.

items.question: Which engines and key features does the AW169 RFM list in the Helicopter general section?
options: Two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW210A engines with dual FADEC, APU mode and variable RPM control, installed in the upper deck under cowlings.
Two Rolls-Royce turboshaft engines with manual fuel controls and fixed RPM.
A single PW210A engine with dual FADEC and a fixed-pitch main rotor.
Two piston engines driving separate main rotors without FADEC.
items.explanation: Section 7 describes the power system as two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW210A engines with dual FADEC, APU mode and variable RPM control capability, installed in the upper deck and covered by cowlings.

items.question: Where is the flotation control panel for the emergency flotation system installed according to the System Description OES section?
options: On the right side of the interseat console in the cockpit.
In the overhead console above the pilots.
On the left cabin sidewall near the sliding door.
On the aft cabin bulkhead next to the baggage door.
items.explanation: The OES System Description states that the flotation control panel is installed on the right side of the interseat console in the cockpit.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-652)

items.question: How does the crew place the emergency flotation system in the armed condition before flight above water?
options: By setting the FLOAT master switch on the flotation control panel to ARMED.
By pulling the guarded FLOAT switch on the collective grip and leaving it raised.
By selecting AUTO EXT on the landing light switch.
By switching off electrical power to both inflation systems.
items.explanation: Section 7 explains that the emergency flotation system operates only when it is in the armed condition, which is achieved by setting the FLOAT master switch on the flotation control panel to ARMED.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-652)

items.question: What does the RFM describe as the primary means of activating the emergency flotation system when it is armed?
options: Automatic actuation via four emergency float switches (water sensors) when two adjacent switches contact water.
Manual activation only by the pilot using a cable pull handle on the floor.
Automatic deployment whenever airspeed falls below 10 kt at low altitude.
Activation solely by the hoist operator using a panel in the cabin.
items.explanation: The OES System Description states that four emergency float switches on the lower fuselage are connected to the flotation control panel and inflation valves and that this automatic water-sensor activation is considered the primary means of emergency flotation system activation when the master switch is ARMED.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-652 to 7-653)

items.question: When does the RFM require the emergency flotation system to be set to ARMED?
options: When the helicopter is in flight above the water.
Whenever the helicopter is parked on the apron.
Only during maintenance ground runs.
Only after the floats have already been deployed in a ditching.
items.explanation: Section 7 notes that the emergency flotation system must be set in the armed condition when the helicopter is in flight above the water.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-653)

items.question: If the automatic activation of the emergency flotation system fails, how can the crew manually inflate the floats according to Section 7?
options: By raising the guard and pressing the guarded FLOAT pushbutton on either the pilot's or co-pilot's collective grip.
By cycling the FLOAT master switch on the interseat console OFF then ARMED three times.
By selecting STOW on the landing light switch for more than five seconds.
By pulling the rotor brake handle fully aft while on the water.
items.explanation: The OES description explains that, in the event of failure of the automatic actuation method, aircrew can command floats inflation via guarded pushbutton FLOAT switches on both pilot and copilot collective grips.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-653)

items.question: What is the purpose of the TEST button on the flotation control panel as described in the System Description?
options: To check the continuity of the electrical circuits from the control panel to the inflation valves and verify that the system test lights illuminate.
To test the rotor brake operation during ground runs.
To simulate a ditching by partially inflating the floats.
To reset all emergency system cautions in the CAS.
items.explanation: Section 7 states that the TEST button on the flotation control panel is used to verify the correct operation and continuity of the electrical circuits to the inflation valves, with the LH SYS and RH SYS lights illuminating during the test.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-653)

items.question: According to the Lights (Chap 33) system description, how are the steerable landing lights normally controlled and what provides backup control?
options: Primarily by switches on the pilot and co-pilot collective grips, with integrated EDCU external lights page controls acting as backup.
Only by the EDCU external lights page; collective grip switches are backup.
Only by a panel on the overhead console with no backup control.
By a floor-mounted pedal, backed up by the hoist operator's panel.
items.explanation: The Lights chapter states that the external lights are controlled via the EDCU lights page, but that the steerable landing lights are primarily controlled via the related switches on the pilot and co-pilot collective grips, with the integrated EDCU controls acting as backup.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Lights (Chap 33) Steerable landing lights (p.7-302 to 7-305)

items.question: With the AW169 landing lights switched off and in the stowed position, what happens when the AUTO EXT/CAGE position is selected on the AUTO EXT/CAGE STOW switch according to the RFM?
options: The selected landing light(s) illuminate and extend automatically to the predefined landing position, and other controls to the light(s) are inhibited during the sequence.
The selected landing light(s) retract and switch off, completing the STOW function.
The selected landing light(s) flash three times and remain stowed for a lamp test only.
The system switches control of the landing lights from the collective grip to the EDCU page.
items.explanation: The steerable landing lights description explains that with the lights switched off and stowed, selecting AUTO EXT/CAGE initiates the AUTO EXT function: the selected light(s) illuminate and extend to the predefined landing position and all other controls to the lights are inhibited during the sequence.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Lights (Chap 33) Steerable landing lights (p.7-305 to 7-307)
